t: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall be used to administer any program which is funded in whole or in part from foreign currencies or credits for which a specific dollar appropriation therefor has not been made.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations restriction barring use of funds to administer programs financed with foreign currencies absent a specific dollar appropriation. The words "program" and "foreign" might suggest outside involvement, but no party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given any right to object or sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall be used to administer any program which is funded in whole or in part from foreign currencies or credits

opus.w: This section only limits spending: appropriated funds can't be used for programs paid for with foreign currencies or credits unless a specific dollar appropriation has been made. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking, or right to sue. The reference to foreign currencies is about where the money comes from. It does not involve any outside party in a federal decision.
opus.b: A possible wrong reading is that the mention of "foreign currencies or credits" brings foreign or outside parties into a federal decision. It doesn't. This is only a limit on how appropriated funds can be used, and no one outside the federal government is consulted or given a role.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a fiscal restriction on the use of federal appropriations. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. The mention of 'foreign currencies' refers to the source of funding, not to a participatory process involving foreign entities.
qwen_chat.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall be used to administer any program which is funded in whole or in part from foreign currencies or credits for which a specific dollar appropriation therefor has not been made.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "foreign currencies or credits" implies interaction with foreign governments or entities, which are outside the federal government. However, the text is a restriction on the use of funds (an appropriations rider) and does not establish a process for consultation, coordination, or participation with those foreign entities. It simply prohibits spending money unless a specific domestic appropriation exists. There is no mechanism described for engaging with outsiders.
